card.text: Hot Jupiter whose dayside heat map JWST measured from its eclipses.

sources.label: Lally et al. 2025
sources.quote: Using two JWST MIRI LRS eclipse observations centered on $8μm$

introduction.text: HD 189733b is a gas giant that circles its star every 2.2 days, always showing it the same face. Its hottest spot lies east of noon.

sources.label: Lally et al. 2025
sources.quote: an unprecedentedly constrained eastward hotspot offset of $33.0^{+0.7}_{-0.9}$ degrees

temperature.title: JWST MIRI map
temperature.summary: The dayside's heat at 8 µm, fitted to eclipses. The hot spot is 33° east of noon; a strip of the night side was never seen.

illustration.title: NASA artist's concept
illustration.summary: The map NASA's Eyes on Exoplanets wraps around this planet. None of it was observed, and its longitudes are arbitrary.
